problem_statement: The shuding/nextra-docs-template documentation site hosts a native "Browse guides by area" guide finder: a docs-home section (also surfaced on the About and Advanced routes) with a row of area tabs (All areas / Getting Started / Guides / Reference) over a grid of guide cards and a live "Showing N of M · <Area>" readout that updates as you pick an area. A regression shipped the finder broken: the area-tab row was pinned to a single fixed-width nowrap strip so the documentation column scrolls sideways on narrow phones, the guide grid collapsed into an overlapping pile of near-illegible cards, the finder was dropped from the About and Advanced routes, and the readout froze so picking an area no longer updates the count. Repair the finder so the tab row wraps within the viewport on mobile, the guide grid reads cleanly, the finder is present on the home, About and Advanced routes, and picking an area re-filters the cards and updates the "Showing N of M · <Area>" readout live.
required_content: Keep the existing Next.js + Nextra + nextra-theme-docs build, the docs Introduction home, the About/Another/Advanced/Satori routes, the counter component demo, and the Nextra navbar/sidebar/TOC chrome intact.

The "Browse guides by area" finder must render its area-tab row fully inside a 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal document overflow beyond a small tolerance (the tabs wrap instead of pinning to one nowrap row).
The guide card grid must read cleanly (no overlapping/shingled cards, legible text) at the desktop and mobile finder breakpoints.
The finder must appear on the Introduction home, the About route AND the Advanced route (a shared docs feature across those three surfaces).
Picking an area tab must re-filter the visible guide cards and update the readout to "Showing N of M · <Area>" for the selected area, not leave the readout frozen on "Showing 6 of 6 · All areas".
design_constraints: Use the existing Next.js + Nextra + MDX architecture and the finder's existing gfinder__* CSS-module classes and data-gfinder-* hooks; do not replace the theme, add a UI framework, or add runtime dependencies.
Keep the guide-card content, area labels, and readout wording repo-native to the template's own routes and theme; do not invent unrelated marketing copy.

The area-tab row must use a wrapping flex layout (flex-wrap:wrap, pill-shaped tabs with rounded corners) rather than a fixed-width nowrap strip, so it reflows within the column width; the guide grid must be a responsive auto-fill grid of rounded rectangular cards with visible gaps and no negative-margin overlap.

The finder must render on-brand: the active area tab and each card's area label use the accent blue (#3056d3) on a light card surface, card titles are dark and legible against the near-white card background, and blurb text has sufficient contrast (no near-white-on-near-white text).

The repaired finder must not introduce horizontal overflow on desktop (1440), tablet (834), or mobile (390) viewports; the tab row wraps to fit the 390px viewport instead of being masked with overflow-x:hidden on a still-oversized row.

Preserve the surrounding Nextra visual chrome — the left sidebar navigation, the right-hand on-page table of contents, the top navbar with the GitHub project link, and the footer text — and keep the counter component demo and every starter route intact.
state_constraints: desktop_home verifies the repaired Introduction home with the Browse-guides-by-area finder, Nextra chrome, and no horizontal overflow.
mobile_home and mobile_finder verify the area-tab row wraps within the 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow (the repaired regression).
tablet_home verifies the repaired page remains readable at the tablet breakpoint.
desktop_finder verifies the finder region (tab row + guide grid + readout) reads cleanly and on-brand at desktop.
desktop_about and desktop_advanced verify the shared finder is present on those two routes as well as home (cross-page continuity).
finder_filter_guides verifies that clicking the Guides area tab re-filters the cards and updates the readout to "Showing 2 of 6 · Guides".
desktop_another protects the original Another Page counter-component route.

change_completion: The area-tab row renders fully inside the mobile viewport with the tabs wrapping instead of overflowing.
Picking an area tab re-filters the guide cards and updates the "Showing N of M · <Area>" readout live.
responsive: The finder has no horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet, or mobile viewports within tolerance.
The guide grid reflows to fit narrow viewports and stays legible on mobile.
regression: The Introduction home, About/Another/Advanced/Satori routes, counter demo, GitHub project link, docsRepositoryBase, and footer text all remain intact.
The Next/Nextra install, build, and start flow still succeeds with no console errors.
design_consistency: The finder keeps native Nextra article typography, the on-brand accent for active tabs and card headings, and a legible card grid.
The repaired finder is present and consistent on the home, About, and Advanced routes.

metadata.design_goal: keep the real repo content, routes, and Nextra chrome intact while repairing a native docs guide-finder that regressed in layout, cross-route presence, and interaction
metadata.source_repo_kind: Next.js Nextra documentation template with MDX pages, a CSS-module guide finder component, theme config, and package metadata
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable docs repo whose home hosts a native Browse-guides-by-area finder; a fixed-width nowrap tab row overflows narrow phones, a collapsed card grid reads illegibly, the finder is missing from secondary routes, and a frozen readout no longer tracks the picked area, giving a precise multi-facet docs repair.

author_notes: Slot slot_254 targets docs / content_asset_continuity / repair / page at L4 on the shuding/nextra-docs-template Nextra documentation template. The native lever is the docs home's own "Browse guides by area" guide finder (a tab-filtered grid of guide cards with a live count readout), surfaced across the home, About, and Advanced routes. The reference wraps the area-tab row responsively, renders a clean on-brand guide-card grid, keeps the finder on all three routes, and re-filters cards + updates the readout on area selection. The known-bad shallow non-fix leaves the tab row a fixed-width nowrap strip (mobile horizontal overflow), collapses the guide-card grid into an overlapping illegible pile with near-white-on-near-white text, drops the finder from the Advanced route, and freezes the readout so the picked area never updates the count. The template's screenshot, counter component, MDX routes, sidebar, TOC, and theme image assets stay intact across every leg.
